lessons.title: GLP-1 in plain words
lessons.summary: These medicines copy a gut hormone: you feel full sooner and think about food less.

points: After a meal, the gut makes a hormone called GLP-1 that tells the brain you are full and slows stomach emptying.
Medicines in this group do the same thing, for longer and more strongly.
Besides GLP-1, tirzepatide also acts on the GIP hormone and, on average, gives more weight loss.
It does not replace healthy eating and exercise; results are best alongside an eating plan and muscle protection.
It is not a short treatment; obesity is a chronic disease and appetite returns when the medicine stops.

lessons.title: Who really needs these medicines?
lessons.summary: Official criteria: a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition.

points: Obesity: BMI of 30 or more.
Overweight: BMI of 27 or more with high blood pressure, diabetes or prediabetes, high lipids, sleep apnea, fatty liver or heart disease.
Type 2 diabetes: for blood-sugar control regardless of weight, with a doctor’s advice.
BMI alone is not enough; a large waist (waist-to-height ratio of 0.5 or more) is a sign of harmful abdominal fat.
If your weight is healthy and you only have a few extra kilos, the side effects can outweigh the benefits.

lessons.source: NICE NG246; NICE TA875 and TA1026; Ashwell 2012

lessons.title: Losing weight without medicine: a 12-week map
lessons.summary: A modest energy deficit, enough protein and strength training: slow but lasting.

points: Eat about 300 to 500 kcal a day below your needs; very low-calorie diets destroy muscle.
Start each meal with protein, then vegetables, and finish with bread or rice.
Fibre from vegetables, fruit with the skin, oats and pulses; enough water through the day.
150 minutes of brisk walking or aerobic activity a week.
2 strength sessions with weights, bands or body weight.
Weigh yourself once a week and measure your waist once a month.
A realistic goal: 0.5 to 1% of your weight a week.
Reassess after 3 months.

lessons.source: WHO 2020 physical activity guidelines; ADA Standards of Care 2025

lessons.title: Protein and muscle: the key point of weight loss
lessons.summary: When appetite drops, the main risk is losing muscle, not fat.

points: During treatment, usually 1.2 to 1.6 g per kg of adjusted body weight; a dietitian sets the exact amount.
25 to 30 g per meal: for example, a palm-sized portion of chicken or fish, or 2 eggs with a cup of yogurt.
Not being hungry is no reason to skip a meal; add a protein snack if needed.
Strength training 2 to 3 times a week is the main protection for muscle.
Discuss losing more than 1.5% of your weight a week with a professional; it usually means under-eating and muscle loss.

lessons.source: Bauer 2013 (PROT-AGE); joint advisory on nutrition with GLP-1 therapy 2025

lessons.title: Eating while on the medicine
lessons.summary: Small regular meals, protein first, eat slowly and drink enough water.

points: Three small regular meals; a protein snack if needed.
Eat slowly and stop at the first feeling of fullness.
At least 8 glasses of water; more in hot weather or with diarrhoea or vomiting.
Cut down heavy fats and fried food, especially in the first days after an injection.
Increase fibre gradually to avoid constipation.
With smaller meals, iron, B12, calcium, vitamin D, zinc and magnesium may run low.
If your intake is very low, ask a dietitian about a multivitamin.

lessons.source: Joint advisory on nutrition with GLP-1 therapy 2025

lessons.title: Common side effects and what to do
lessons.summary: Most side effects are digestive, worse in the first weeks and after each dose increase, and they ease over time.

points: Nausea: small low-fat meals, fluids between meals, ginger or dry crackers.
Constipation: more water, gradual fibre, walking.
Diarrhoea: water and oral rehydration solution, temporarily less fat.
Heartburn: do not lie down for 2 to 3 hours after eating; avoid fizzy drinks.
Hair loss: usually linked to fast weight loss and it grows back; eat enough protein.
Nausea for more than a week, or being unable to eat.
Diarrhoea for more than 24 hours, or constipation for more than 3 to 4 days.
If side effects are heavy, the doctor can delay the next dose increase.

lessons.source: Wegovy and Zepbound prescribing information; STEP 1; SURMOUNT-1

lessons.title: Warning signs: get help now
lessons.summary: These signs are rare but serious; if you notice them, skip the dose and get medical help right away (call your local emergency number).

points: Severe, constant pain in the upper abdomen that spreads to the back (possible pancreatitis).
Pain in the upper right abdomen, fever or yellow skin (gallbladder).
Vomiting or diarrhoea for more than 24 hours with little urine and dizziness (dehydration and kidney injury).
Swelling of the face, lips or throat, or trouble breathing (severe allergy).
Severe abdominal pain with bloating and not passing gas (bowel obstruction).
A lump in the neck, hoarseness or trouble swallowing.
Severe low mood or thoughts of self-harm (contact a crisis line now).

lessons.title: Starting treatment and realistic expectations
lessons.summary: The dose goes up in small steps; the first doses are for getting used to it, not for weight loss.

points: Tirzepatide: 2.5 → 5 → 7.5 → 10 → 12.5 → 15 mg, at least every 4 weeks.
Semaglutide for obesity: 0.25 → 0.5 → 1 → 1.7 → 2.4 mg, every 4 weeks.
Liraglutide: 0.6 to 3 mg daily, one step each week.
In trials, over about one to one and a half years, average loss was about 8% with liraglutide, about 15% with semaglutide 2.4 mg and about 20% with high-dose tirzepatide.
These are averages; individual responses vary.

lessons.title: Buying safely, storage and missed doses
lessons.summary: Only from a licensed pharmacy, with a prescription.

points: Buy only from a licensed pharmacy with a prescription; avoid gyms, beauty clinics and online sellers.
Unlicensed and “compounded” copies may contain the wrong dose or other substances.
Never share a pen with anyone, even with a new needle.
Keep unused pens in the fridge (2 to 8 °C), away from the freezer.
Tirzepatide: take a missed dose if it is within 4 days, otherwise skip it. Semaglutide: within 5 days.
Never take two doses together.

lessons.title: Stopping the medicine and weight regain
lessons.summary: When the medicine stops, appetite returns and most people regain part of the weight.

points: In withdrawal trials, most participants regained a large part of the lost weight within a year.
These medicines work more like treatment for a chronic disease than a short course.
Before starting, plan for at least a year of cost.
Build eating habits and strength training from the first month.
Reduce or stop the medicine gradually with your doctor, not suddenly.

lessons.title: Benefits beyond weight
lessons.summary: In some conditions, these medicines help beyond weight loss.

points: In people with obesity and heart disease, semaglutide reduced cardiovascular events (SELECT trial).
Semaglutide slowed kidney disease in diabetes (FLOW) and is approved for inflammatory fatty liver disease.
Tirzepatide is approved for sleep apnea with obesity.

lessons.title: Pregnancy, breastfeeding and these medicines
lessons.summary: They are not used in pregnancy or breastfeeding and must be stopped before trying to conceive.

points: Semaglutide is usually stopped at least 2 months before trying to conceive.
If you become pregnant while taking it, stop the medicine and tell your doctor.
During this time the goal is not weight loss; enough nutrition and normal pregnancy weight gain matter, and a dietitian can help.

lessons.title: The contraceptive pill and tirzepatide
lessons.summary: Tirzepatide may make the oral contraceptive pill less effective.

points: For the first 4 weeks and for 4 weeks after each dose increase, use a backup method (such as condoms) or a non-oral method.
Talk to a gynaecologist about the best method for you.

lessons.title: The thyroid and medullary cancer
lessons.summary: A personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2 is a contraindication.

points: This contraindication is based on animal findings and covers every medicine in this group.
An underactive or overactive thyroid, or a simple nodule, is not a contraindication, but tell your doctor.
If you do not know which thyroid cancer runs in your family, find out before starting.
Report a neck lump, hoarseness or trouble swallowing right away.

lessons.title: Low blood sugar with insulin and diabetes tablets
lessons.summary: On their own these medicines rarely lower blood sugar too much, but with insulin or glibenclamide there is a risk.

points: Before starting, your doctor should review your insulin or diabetes tablet dose.
Signs of low blood sugar: shaking, sweating, confusion, a racing heart.
If your sugar is low: a glass of fruit juice or 3 sugar cubes, then check again after 15 minutes.
Do not skip meals.

lessons.title: Surgery, endoscopy and anaesthesia
lessons.summary: These medicines slow stomach emptying, so fasting before anaesthesia may need to change.

points: Always tell your surgeon and anaesthetist that you take this medicine.
The decision to pause it or change fasting belongs to the anaesthesia team.
It is better to start the medicine after the operation.

lessons.title: Pancreas, gallbladder and kidneys
lessons.summary: A history of disease in these organs is not an absolute contraindication, but the decision is the doctor’s, with close follow-up.

points: Pancreatitis: with severe abdominal pain the medicine is stopped and checked; with a history of pancreatitis, use with caution or not at all.
Gallbladder: fast weight loss raises the risk of gallstones.
Kidneys: vomiting and diarrhoea with dehydration can harm the kidneys; enough water and a creatinine test matter.

lessons.title: Emotional eating and mood
lessons.summary: Eating disorders and depression should be assessed and treated separately before medical treatment.

points: These medicines reduce appetite and, with an eating disorder, may strengthen an unhealthy pattern.
If your mood gets worse during treatment, tell your doctor.
A psychologist or psychiatrist can help alongside your eating plan.
If you have thoughts of harming yourself, contact your local emergency number or a crisis line now.

lessons.title: Teenagers and weight-loss medicines
lessons.summary: From 12 to 17, only some medicines, and only under a paediatrician or paediatric endocrinologist.

points: In teenagers, weight is judged by BMI-for-age percentile, not adult numbers.
Growth, puberty and enough nutrition come first; strict dieting is harmful.
A family eating and activity plan is the base of treatment.

lessons.title: Snoring, sleep apnea and weight
lessons.summary: Loud snoring with daytime sleepiness can be a sign of sleep apnea.

points: Sleep apnea is linked with high blood pressure, heart disease and difficulty losing weight.
It is diagnosed with a sleep study; talk to your doctor.
Weight loss improves sleep apnea, and tirzepatide is approved for sleep apnea with obesity.
